title: World Geography — Introduction and Tools
description: Master advanced geographic tools and the five themes for world geography study.
objectives: Apply five themes to case studies
Use latitude, longitude, and time zones
Interpret multiple map projections

lessons.title: Map Projections
lessons.content: Representing a sphere on a flat map always involves distortion.
examples: Mercator: preserves shape and angles but distorts size (Greenland appears as large as Africa!)
Peters/Gall-Peters: accurate area but distorts shape
Robinson: compromise projection used for world maps
Goode's Homolosine: interrupts ocean to minimize land distortion

lessons.title: Time Zones
lessons.content: Earth is divided into 24 time zones (roughly 15° longitude each).
examples: When it's noon in New York (EST = UTC-5), it's 5pm in London (UTC+0) and 1am in Tokyo (UTC+9)
International Date Line (180° longitude): crossing west to east: lose a day
China uses a single time zone despite spanning 5 geographical zones

title: North America — In Depth
description: In-depth regional geography of North America.
objectives: Analyze regional differences within North America
Explain USMCA and its geographic effects
Describe environmental challenges shared by North American nations

lessons.title: Regional Analysis
lessons.content: North America has remarkable regional diversity within three major nations.
examples: U.S. Sun Belt vs. Rust Belt: demographic and economic shift since 1970
Canadian provinces: Quebec (French-speaking, distinct culture), Alberta (oil sands), British Columbia (Pacific economy)
Mexico: sharp contrast between industrialized north (maquiladoras) and rural, indigenous south

title: Latin America — In Depth
description: Study the physical, cultural, and economic geography of Latin America.
objectives: Describe Latin America's physical geography in depth
Analyze urbanization in Latin America
Evaluate economic challenges and opportunities

lessons.title: Megacities
lessons.content: Latin America is one of the world's most urbanized regions.
examples: São Paulo: 22 million; Brazil's economic engine; extreme inequality (Gini coefficient ~0.48)
Mexico City: 22 million; built on ancient lake bed; sinks 10 inches/year
Lima: 10+ million; 70% arrived through rural migration in last 50 years

lessons.title: Economic Geography
lessons.content: Latin America is rich in resources but faces structural economic challenges.
examples: Commodity dependence: copper (Chile, Peru), soy (Brazil, Argentina), oil (Venezuela, Mexico)
Dutch Disease: resource exports can strengthen currency, hurting manufacturing exports
Inequality: Latin America is the world's most unequal region; Gini coefficients among world's highest

title: Europe — In Depth
description: Advanced study of European geography — physical, political, and economic.
objectives: Explain the Brexit decision geographically
Describe the refugee crisis of 2015 and its geographic dimensions
Analyze Europe's energy geography

lessons.title: Brexit Geography
lessons.content: The UK's vote to leave the EU had clear geographic patterns.
examples: England's post-industrial cities (Sunderland, Stoke) voted heavily Leave; London and Scotland voted Remain
Northern Ireland: Good Friday Agreement required open border with Republic of Ireland — Brexit threatened this
The 'two Britains': cosmopolitan, educated cities vs. left-behind post-industrial towns

lessons.title: Energy Geography
lessons.content: Europe faces a major energy transition challenge.
examples: Germany: Energiewende — transition to renewable energy; closed nuclear plants; became dependent on Russian gas
Nord Stream 2 pipeline: geopolitical tool; destroyed 2022 after Russia invaded Ukraine
North Sea wind: massive offshore wind capacity; UK, Denmark, Netherlands leading

title: Middle East and North Africa — In Depth
description: Advanced study of MENA geography, resources, and geopolitics.
objectives: Analyze oil's role in shaping MENA
Describe water scarcity challenges
Evaluate ongoing geopolitical conflicts

lessons.title: Oil Geography
lessons.content: The Persian Gulf holds 60% of proven world oil reserves — making it strategically vital.
examples: Saudi Arabia: world's largest oil exporter; Ghawar field — largest in the world
OPEC: oil cartel that manages production to influence prices
Gulf states using oil wealth to diversify (Dubai, Abu Dhabi): tourism, finance, technology
Petrodollar recycling: Gulf states reinvest oil revenues in Western financial systems

lessons.title: Water Wars
lessons.content: Water scarcity is creating serious geopolitical tensions in MENA.
examples: Nile: Ethiopia's Grand Renaissance Dam threatens Egypt's water supply — potential for conflict
Jordan River: shared by Israel, Jordan, Palestine — severely over-extracted
Aquifer depletion: Saudi Arabia depleted 'fossil' aquifers for wheat production in 1970s–90s — now stops

title: Sub-Saharan Africa — In Depth
description: Advanced study of Sub-Saharan Africa's geography, economy, and potential.
objectives: Analyze Africa's 'resource curse' in depth
Describe Africa's youthful demography and its implications
Evaluate Africa's technological leapfrogging

lessons.title: Africa's Economic Geography
lessons.content: Africa has vast resources but structural barriers to development.
examples: DRC: holds ~70% of world's cobalt — essential for EV batteries; yet one of world's poorest countries
Nigeria: Africa's largest economy; oil accounts for 90% of exports — extreme volatility
'Africa Rising': decade of 5%+ growth in many countries (2000–2015)

lessons.title: Demographic Dividend
lessons.content: Africa's youthful population could be its greatest asset — or its biggest challenge.
examples: Africa will have 2 billion people by 2050; median age just 19
If young people are educated and employed: demographic dividend → rapid growth (as seen in East Asia)
If not: youth unemployment → instability → migration pressure

title: South and East Asia — In Depth
description: Advanced study of South and East Asian geography, economy, and geopolitics.
objectives: Analyze China's Belt and Road Initiative
Describe South Asia's water security challenges
Evaluate East Asian economic geography

lessons.title: China's Belt and Road Initiative
lessons.content: China's $1 trillion+ infrastructure investment program is reshaping global geography.
examples: BRI: loans and construction in 150+ countries for roads, ports, railways, pipelines
Gwadar Port (Pakistan): Chinese-built deep-water port gives China access to Indian Ocean
Critics: 'debt trap diplomacy' — Sri Lanka gave up Hambantota Port for 99 years when it couldn't repay loans
Supporters: fills infrastructure gap developing countries desperately need

lessons.title: East Asian Economic Geography
lessons.content: East Asia has achieved remarkable economic development through export-led growth.
examples: Japan (1960s–80s), South Korea and Taiwan (1970s–90s), China (1980s–2000s): each followed similar export-led model
Special Economic Zones: China's SEZs (Shenzhen, Shanghai) attracted foreign investment with tax benefits
Taiwan: semiconductor manufacturing hub; TSMC makes chips used in ~90% of advanced devices worldwide

title: Pacific World — Oceania and Antarctica
description: Study the Pacific world, from the island nations to Antarctica.
objectives: Analyze Pacific Island geography and culture
Describe Antarctica's geography and international governance
Evaluate the Pacific as a geopolitical arena

lessons.title: Pacific Island Nations
lessons.content: The Pacific Islands are among the most culturally rich and geographically threatened places on Earth.
examples: Polynesia, Micronesia, Melanesia: thousands of islands across a third of Earth's surface
Traditional navigation: Polynesian wayfinders used stars, ocean swells, birds, and clouds to navigate thousands of miles
Climate crisis: Kiribati, Tuvalu, Marshall Islands face complete inundation by 2100 at current sea level rise rates

lessons.title: Antarctica
lessons.content: Antarctica is governed by the unique Antarctic Treaty System.
examples: Antarctic Treaty (1959): 54 countries agree to peaceful scientific use only — no military, no mining
Antarctica is the world's only continent without a permanent human population or national sovereignty claims (frozen by treaty)
Ice sheets: hold 70% of world's fresh water; West Antarctic Ice Sheet melting faster than expected

title: Cultural Geography — Language and Religion
description: Advanced study of cultural geography — language, religion, and cultural landscapes.
objectives: Map world language families
Analyze how religion shapes geography
Study cultural landscape analysis

lessons.title: Language Geography
lessons.content: Languages cluster in families and reflect historical migrations and contacts.
examples: Indo-European family: covers Europe, Iran, northern India — all descended from a proto-language ~5,000 BCE
Bantu expansion: single language family spread from West Africa across sub-Saharan Africa ~3,000 years ago
Language loss: 50% of world's 7,000 languages may be extinct by 2100; with them, irreplaceable knowledge

lessons.title: Religion and Landscape
lessons.content: Religion shapes everything from architecture to law to land use.
examples: Sacred sites as geographic anchors: Jerusalem, Mecca, Varanasi, Vatican, Uluru
Religious law and land use: halal/kosher restrictions shape agriculture and trade
Pilgrimage geography: Mecca receives 2+ million pilgrims during Hajj — enormous logistical and environmental challenge

title: Global Geography — Interconnected World
description: Synthesize geographic understanding to analyze the interconnected challenges of the modern world.
objectives: Apply geographic thinking to global challenges
Evaluate geographic solutions
Propose evidence-based geographic policies

lessons.title: Interconnected Challenges
lessons.content: Today's biggest challenges require geographic thinking to understand and solve.
examples: Pandemic geography: COVID spread along airline routes; unequal vaccine access follows wealth geography
Supply chain geography: COVID disruptions revealed over-concentration of manufacturing in China
Climate-migration nexus: 216 million internal climate migrants projected by 2050 (World Bank)

lessons.title: Your Geographic Toolkit
lessons.content: You now have the tools to analyze any geographic situation.
examples: Five Themes: apply Location, Place, Region, Movement, HEI to any issue
Scale: always ask 'at what scale?' — local, national, global perspectives give different insights
Systems thinking: trace connections between physical and human geography
Spatial thinking: maps reveal patterns invisible in tables or text
